jobs.title: Creative Operations Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Creative Operations Manager to be the operational backbone of Perplexity's creative team. Our creative output is scaling fast — brand campaigns, GTM launches, shoots, partnerships — and we need someone who can run the production of all of it so our designers, motion designers, and brand leads can stay focused on the creative work.



You'll be the connective tissue between creative vision and real-world execution: coordinating projects across multiple teams, managing vendors and contractors, organizing shoots, and handling the licenses and contracts that keep everything legitimate and on track. You know how to protect creative intent while keeping timelines grounded in reality.



You'll report into the Brand/Creative Studio team and partner daily with Brand, Motion, Web, and our cross-functional partners in Comms, Product Marketing, and Partnerships.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Coordinate creative projects across multiple teams — owning scopes, timelines, budgets, and delivery so nothing falls through the gaps

 - Be the single point of contact for cross-functional partners (Comms, Product Marketing, Partnerships, Events) so requests are triaged, scoped, and delivered

 - Source and manage vendors, contractors, freelancers, and external agencies — negotiating, briefing, and keeping relationships strong

 - Organize and run shoots end-to-end: casting, location scouting, scheduling, crewing, and on-set logistics

 - Own licenses, contracts, releases, and rights management — keeping the team compliant and unblocked

 - Build and run a production workflow and intake process that keeps a fast-moving creative team organized without adding bureaucracy

 - Partner with post-production to make sure final assets are delivered on time and to spec

 - Protect the team's focus — handle the operational weight so creatives can do their best work


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience as a producer on an in-house creative or brand team (e.g., Brand Producer / Creative Producer), ideally at a tech or consumer software company

 - A track record coordinating creative projects across teams and keeping them on time, on budget, and on brand

 - Hands-on experience managing vendors, contractors, and agencies, including negotiating and managing contracts

 - Experience organizing shoots — photo and video — and handling the logistics, licensing, and releases that come with them

 - Strong program and project management instincts; you bring order to a fast, ambiguous environment

 - Excellent communication and stakeholder management — you keep a lot of people aligned without slowing them down

 - Fluency with creative tools and workflows (Figma, Adobe Creative Suite) and the production process from concept to delivery

 - Comfort working alongside strong creative leaders — this role is about enabling great creative work, not directing it


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience standing up production processes and intake systems from scratch

 - Background in both brand/campaign production and event or experiential production

 - A network of trusted vendors, photographers, directors, and production partners

jobs.title: GTM Strategy & Operations Lead
jobs.description:
Perplexity is seeking a GTM Strategy & Operations Lead to join our Enterprise team. In this role, you will own the analytical and operational foundation of our sales organization, working directly with the VP of Sales and front-line sales leaders across all of our sales motions. This role is ideal for a hands-on operator who has helped a sales organization grow through its messiest stages and wants to build the planning, forecasting, and performance infrastructure for one of the fastest-growing enterprise businesses in AI.

This is an individual contributor role reporting to the VP of Sales

Responsibilities

 - Run the GTM operating cadence, including weekly pipeline reviews, forecast calls, and quarterly business reviews, owning both the underlying data and the narrative

 - Build and own the sales forecasting process, giving leadership an accurate and defensible view of the quarter

 - Design and maintain territory and segment models across all sales motions, and own the territory carve process

 - Build sales capacity, coverage, and quota models that connect hiring plans to revenue targets

 - Own performance reporting across the funnel: conversion, pipeline health, rep productivity, attainment, and ramp

 - Conduct strategic analyses to identify where the business is working and where it is not, and turn findings into clear recommendations for sales leadership

 - Drive high-priority cross-functional GTM initiatives, from annual planning through execution

 - Partner with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Strategic Finance to keep the go-to-market plan grounded in shared data

Qualifications

 - Significant experience in GTM strategy, sales operations, revenue operations, or a similar function at a high-growth company, with direct exposure to what breaks as a sales team scales and a record of fixing it

 - Strong SQL and hands-on analytical skills; you pull your own data and build your own models rather than waiting on analyst support

 - Deep familiarity with Salesforce and experience working directly in a data warehouse such as Snowflake

 - Proven ability to run an operating cadence with senior sales leaders and hold the organization to it

 - Skilled at structuring ambiguous problems and communicating recommendations clearly to executives

 - Comfortable moving between long-range planning and same-day operational questions

 - Exceptional written and verbal communication; comfortable presenting to senior stakeholders

 - Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience

Nice to Haves

 - Experience operating a usage-based or consumption business model, where forecasting and planning go beyond seat counts

 - Background in management consulting, strategic finance, or corporate strategy prior to an operating role

 - Experience at an AI or enterprise infrastructure company

jobs.title: AI Strategist, Legal
jobs.description:
Perplexity is an AI-powered answer engine founded in December 2022 and growing rapidly as one of the world's leading AI platforms. Perplexity has raised over $1B in venture investment from some of the world's most visionary and successful leaders, including Elad Gil, Daniel Gross, Jeff Bezos, Accel, IVP, NEA, NVIDIA, Samsung, and many more. Our objective is to build accurate, trustworthy AI that powers decision-making for people and assistive AI wherever decisions are being made.



Throughout human history, change and innovation have always been driven by curious people. Today, curious people use Perplexity to answer more than 780 million queries every month—a number that's growing rapidly for one simple reason: everyone can be curious.



ABOUT THE ROLE

Perplexity is building the AI platform for professional legal work: Perplexity Computer, our agentic platform that navigates tools, completes multi-step workflows, and connects to the case law, statutes, filings, contracts, and internal documents that legal professionals already rely on, and our API Platform, which powers search, retrieval, and automation across structured and unstructured legal data.



At the center of this is our Applied AI / Forward Deployed motion: we work closely with law firms and in-house legal teams to distill their core legal processes and embed them into bespoke solutions built on our platform. That means sitting with partners, associates, and counsel to understand how they research, review, draft, and advise, then translating those workflows into custom skills, agents, and connector configurations that run inside their daily process—and feeding what we learn back into the product so it compounds across customers.



As an AI Strategist on our Applied AI team focused on the legal vertical, you are the subject matter expert who makes this real for legal professionals. This is a commercial and sales engineering role: you will own strategic customer engagements end to end—leading discovery, defining what to build, demonstrating frontier capabilities against real legal workflows, and driving deployments from first conversation through production and expansion. You are part customer owner, part product strategist, part sales engineer—fluent in both the language of the practice group and the language of the platform.


RESPONSIBILITIES


OWN STRATEGIC LEGAL ENGAGEMENTS

 - Lead discovery with law firms and in-house legal departments: what matters to the practice, what problems they are solving, and which workflows are worth automating

 - Define scope—what is the right thing to build—and own success metrics, pilot design, and commercial structure

 - Drive deployment and rollout across practice groups and legal departments, with real revenue responsibility alongside Sales


BE THE DEMO AND TECHNICAL PROOF ENGINE

 - Build and deliver compelling, workflow-specific demonstrations: legal research, contract review and analysis, due diligence, drafting, deposition and discovery summarization, regulatory monitoring

 - Prototype workflows, skills, and connector configurations hands-on in Perplexity Computer and the API Platform to prove value in the customer's own use cases

 - Run pilots and evaluations that hold up to scrutiny from skeptical partners and general counsel


BRING DOMAIN JUDGMENT TO THE PRODUCT

 - Translate how practice groups, legal departments, and legal ops teams actually work into product, connector, and data-partnership priorities

 - Assess whether we have the right research, contract, docket, and document-management integrations to serve each legal segment—and drive the roadmap where we do not

 - Codify repeatable engagement patterns: discovery templates, practice-specific reference workflows, demo libraries, and deployment playbooks


OPERATE AS THE COMMERCIAL LEAD

 - Own senior relationships with partners, general counsel, and legal-innovation leaders; move engagements through qualification, scoping, proposal, pricing, legal, and close

 - Create urgency, write crisp follow-ups, and know when to push and when to wait


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3+ years of direct experience practicing law at a leading firm or in-house—litigation, transactional, or regulatory—or in legal ops / legal innovation with deep workflow exposure; you have run diligence, drafted and negotiated agreements, and lived the workflows you will now automate

 - 5+ years of total experience spanning legal and some combination of technical GTM, sales engineering, solutions architecture, AI product strategy, or applied AI with customer exposure

 - Deep fluency in legal workflows: research, contract review, diligence, drafting, discovery, regulatory analysis, and matter management

 - Strong intuition for AI products, agents, and workflows, with the ability to understand technical systems without needing every detail pre-digested

 - Demonstrated ability to turn ambiguous customer problems into scoped, executable deployment plans with clear success metrics

 - Strong commercial instincts and comfort operating with partners, general counsel, CIOs, and heads of innovation

 - Excellent written and verbal communication; able to write proposals, customer memos, technical scopes, and launch narratives

 - High agency and low ego, with the ability to run multiple complex customer workstreams in parallel and make progress before the playbook exists


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - JD and bar admission

 - Hands-on experience building with agentic systems, tool-use workflows, MCP, or LLM APIs

 - Working knowledge of legal technology platforms: Westlaw, LexisNexis, iManage, NetDocuments, Relativity, Ironclad, or similar

 - Experience selling or deploying technology into law firms or regulated enterprises, including outside-counsel guidelines, privilege, and security review

 - Founder or early-startup operating experience

 - Strong network across AmLaw 100 firms and Fortune 500 legal departments



If you're excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't match every qualification listed above.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Talent Acquisition
jobs.description:
Perplexity is scaling at a pace few companies ever experience, and talent is the surface where our biggest bets get won or lost. We're hiring a Program Manager to sit at the center of that motion, owning the mission-critical, cross-functional programs that shape how we plan, prioritize, and hire.

This is a uniquely visible seat, reserved for operators who thrive in ambiguity and have a track record of driving companywide initiatives to measurable outcomes. You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with recruiting leadership, executives, and cross-functional partners to architect the systems, operating rhythms, and decision-making frameworks that let the company move faster and with more clarity. When a complex, high-stakes program needs an owner, you're the person leadership turns to.


What You'll Do

 - Own Perplexity's most consequential talent programs end-to-end, from ambiguous mandate to shipped outcome

 - Partner directly with executives and recruiting leadership to turn strategy into programs with clear owners, milestones, and accountability

 - Drive cross-functional initiatives across Recruiting, People, Finance, and business leadership, aligning stakeholders and clearing blockers before they escalate

 - Design the operating cadence of the org: planning cycles, prioritization, reporting rhythms, and executive updates that keep leadership decisive

 - Build the systems, tooling, and workflows that let recruiting scale, automating the repetitive so human judgment goes to the highest-leverage work

 - Stand up the metrics and dashboards that turn hiring data into faster, sharper decisions

 - Anticipate risk on the highest-visibility programs, communicate crisply under pressure, and drive to resolution when priorities shift

 - Set the bar for program excellence and codify repeatable playbooks the rest of the company can adopt

What You Bring

 - 7+ years of program or project management experience, including ownership of companywide, mission-critical initiatives

 - Direct experience partnering with and presenting to executives on high-stakes, cross-functional work

 - Track record of driving ambiguous programs to measurable outcomes in fast-paced, rapidly scaling environments

 - Operational rigor. You build order out of chaos and design systems that outlast you

 - Strong analytical instincts, with the ability to structure messy data into clear direction for leadership

 - Sharp communication and stakeholder judgment, with the discretion to operate on sensitive, high-visibility work

 - A builder's mindset and a bias for action, aligned with Perplexity's ethos of building what hasn't been built before

 - Recruiting, talent, or People-org program experience is a plus, but we're optimizing for the best operators first

jobs.title: Business Operations Manager, Marketing and Communications
jobs.description:
Perplexity is scaling at a pace few companies experience, and the Communications and Marketing team is growing with it. We're hiring a Business Operations Manager to build and run the operating system underneath, so an incredibly busy team can move fast and stay in lockstep.

That means keeping the wheels turning: the tool stack, agencies and vendors, budgets, contracts, and the dashboards leadership relies on. It also means building what doesn't exist yet, and making sure everyone knows what's happening and nothing gets dropped. Half builder, half connective tissue. If you like turning ideas into things people use every day, this role is for you.

What you'll do

 - Own the marketing and comms tool stack: evaluate, procure, onboard, provision access, train the team, and retire what we've outgrown

 - Build and maintain internal tools such as calendars, intake forms, dashboards, trackers, and automations, and keep them reliable as more people depend on them

 - Run the team's operating rhythm: priorities, launch and campaign calendars, planning cycles, and the cross-functional handoffs that carry work from idea to launch without dropped threads

 - Manage agencies, contractors, and vendors from selection and onboarding through scopes, invoices, renewals, and performance

 - Keep contracts and procurement moving with Legal and Finance so agreements never become the bottleneck

 - Be the connective tissue across the team: know who's working on what, spot dependencies early, and keep people aligned without adding meetings

 - Act as a thought partner and triage point to leadership: keep them informed, spot problems early, know when to escalate, propose solutions, and see them through

 - Add rigor without slowing anyone down, knowing the difference between process that helps and process that's overhead

What you bring

 - 4-7 years in marketing operations, business operations, or a similar systems-and-process role, ideally in a fast-growing technology company

 - You build things. You've stood up tools, automations, or dashboards yourself, and AI tools are already part of how you work

 - Strong analytical instincts, able to turn messy inputs into numbers leadership can trust

 - Experience managing agency, contractor, or vendor relationships and working with Legal and Finance on contracts and procurement

 - Exceptionally organized and genuinely relational. People like working with you, tell you things early, and trust you with what's really going on

 - A clear, direct communicator who can brief an executive, run a cross-functional meeting, and write a process doc people actually follow

 - Demonstrated experience working closely with and as a trusted partner to senior executives

 - Comfortable in ambiguity and thinks in scale, building things that hold up when the team, budget, or number of launches doubles

 - No specific tool stack required. You've operated marketing or comms systems in a high-growth environment and can pick ours up fast

jobs.title: Strategic Finance Lead - Compute
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Strategic Finance Lead for our GPU compute fleet. In this role, you will be a key partner to our inference and infrastructure teams, providing financial expertise to optimize our compute investments and drive capacity decisions.



In this role, you'll develop deep expertise in the economics of AI compute, from token-level serving cost to the long-range financial planning of our GPU fleet. You'll build the models that inform Perplexity's capacity and make-versus-buy decisions, own the internal-cost analysis that underpins internal and external token pricing, and translate complex infrastructure dynamics into clear financial narratives for leadership.



This is a high-impact role for someone who thrives at the intersection of finance and infrastructure, and who is energized by building frameworks from scratch in a fast-moving environment.



This position is based in San Francisco and requires in-person attendance 2-3 days per week.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Finance lead for GPU compute spend, including budgeting, monthly forecasting, variance analysis, and financial plan maintenance

 - Build and maintain detailed bottoms-up financial models for the GPU fleet, including capacity forecasts, cost driver analyses, and investment scenario modeling

 - Develop deep expertise in GPU vendor contracts, pricing structures, and cost drivers, and surface optimization opportunities across the fleet

 - Serve as subject matter expert for Perplexity's compute capacity plan, owning source of truth on utilization, committed-versus-consumed spend, and capacity by vendor and cluster

 - Build internal token-cost curves distinguishing marginal from fully loaded serving cost, and translate them into internal and external token pricing

 - Analyze the ROI of in-house inference and training, including opportunity cost across chip types, cluster configurations, and workloads, distilled into a framework for capacity deployment

 - Partner closely with inference and infrastructure engineering to understand how serving and training workloads scale, and translate those technical dynamics into financial frameworks


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE

 - Exceptional analytical skills with an ability to synthesize data into compelling insights and develop complex financial operating models

 - Extraordinary problem-solving and critical thinking abilities to develop new frameworks for assessing utilization and capital efficiency in a rapidly evolving industry

 - Attention to detail and patience for getting to the source of truth on complex and interconnected contract and usage data

 - Comfort being the finance person in the room with engineering leads and vendor counterparts, and adept at communicating complex financial information to non-finance audiences

 - A proven track record of partnering with technical teams to drive financial optimization initiatives, building enough trust to become indispensable to their roadmap and resourcing decisions

 - A bias toward action, strong work ethic, and experience driving operational outcomes under tight timelines

 - Background in AI, ML, or high-performance, large-scale computing infrastructure, including data centers and cloud service providers


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years of experience in strategic finance, infrastructure investment, private equity, growth equity, consulting, or investment banking, preferably with infrastructure or datacenter experience

 - Experience in cloud or GPU infrastructure financial management, including direct work with major cloud service providers or neoclouds

 - Direct experience with committed-use economics — reserved capacity, savings plans, committed-use discounts — and GPU procurement

 - Deep expertise in GPU vendor economics, contract structures, and pricing models

 - Experience with chip architecture economics and optimization strategies

 - Proficiency with financial modeling tools

jobs.title: Strategic Finance Lead - AI

In this role, you'll develop deep expertise in the unit economics of AI products, from per-request serving cost to consolidated product-level margin across our portfolio. You'll build the models that inform Perplexity's pricing, packaging, and model-deployment decisions, own the product-margin methodology that reconciles revenue and inference cost from production data, and translate complex model economics into clear financial narratives for leadership.



This is a high-impact role for someone who thrives at the intersection of finance and AI product strategy, and who is energized by building frameworks from scratch in a fast-moving environment.



This position is based in San Francisco and requires in-person attendance 2-3 days per week.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Finance lead for inference and model spend, including budgeting, monthly forecasting, variance analysis, and financial plan maintenance

 - Build and maintain product-margin models across the product portfolio, reconciling revenue, serving cost, and gross margin from production usage data

 - Develop deep expertise in model provider contracts, pricing structures, and cost drivers, and surface optimization opportunities across the model portfolio and routing mix

 - Serve as subject matter expert for product unit economics, owning source of truth on cost per request, margin by product and tier, and customer-segment and feature-level economics

 - Own the consolidated model-cost forecast, translating product roadmaps and model transitions into forward-looking spend and margin trajectories

 - Analyze the margin impact of pricing, packaging, and model-deployment decisions, distilled into a framework for product and pricing strategy

 - Partner closely with product, inference, and data engineering to understand how usage and serving cost scale, and translate those technical dynamics into financial frameworks


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE

 - Exceptional analytical skills with an ability to synthesize data into compelling insights and develop complex financial operating models

 - Extraordinary problem-solving and critical thinking abilities to develop new frameworks for assessing product margin and unit economics in a rapidly evolving industry

 - Attention to detail and patience for getting to the source of truth on complex and interconnected usage, revenue, and cost data

 - Comfort working cross-functionally and are adept at communicating complex financial information to non-finance audiences

 - Sound commercial judgment across pricing, packaging, discounting, and the tradeoffs between growth and margin

 - A proven track record of partnering with technical and product teams to drive financial optimization initiatives

 - A bias toward action, strong work ethic, and experience driving operational outcomes under tight timelines

 - Background in AI, ML, or consumption-based business models with complex cost structures


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years of experience in strategic finance, private equity, growth equity, consulting, or investment banking, preferably with software or AI product experience

 - Experience in AI or LLM product financial management, including direct work with model providers or inference platforms

 - Deep expertise in usage-based pricing, subscription economics, and gross-margin and COGS attribution by customer and model family

 - Experience with model serving economics, including how latency, throughput, and token usage flow through to margin performance

 - Proficiency with financial modeling tools

jobs.title: Strategic Business Operations Lead, API
jobs.description:
Perplexity's API Platform brings our work in AI, search, and agent orchestration to developers. Our customers range from AI-native startups to some of the world's largest technology companies. Working with them, alongside our own developments in building Perplexity’s core application gives our team direct exposure to how search, models, and tools are used to build and scale AI-native products and applications.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

We are looking for a Strategic Business Operations Lead to manage customer relationships and lead projects that help grow the API business. The role is roughly half customer-facing and half strategic and operational work, with an initial focus on building and improving our post-sale programs.



You will own a portfolio of API customers, learning how AI-native companies and large enterprises evaluate, adopt, and scale AI infrastructure. Working closely with API leadership, you will help shape how the business operates and lead projects such as product migrations, customer enablement, and account coverage. You will put recommendations into practice, with results measured in customer adoption, retention, and growth.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Manage a portfolio of API customer relationships, leading account conversations, understanding business priorities, and coordinating next steps across technical and commercial teams.

 - Build account plans around adoption, value, and growth. Identify risks early and partner with Sales and account owners on renewals and expansion.

 - Design and improve the post-sale operating model, including customer segmentation, account coverage, onboarding, health signals, and handoffs between teams.

 - Lead strategic projects across the API business, with an initial emphasis on customer adoption and retention. Scope the problem, develop a recommendation, coordinate execution, and track outcomes.

 - Run customer programs such as product and endpoint migrations, enablement, and rollout communications. Establish the audience, milestones, internal responsibilities, and follow-up needed for each.

 - Coordinate customer communications for product updates, pricing changes, deprecations, and incidents, working with Engineering, Support, and commercial teams on accurate messaging.

 - Analyze usage, consumption against commitments, renewal risk, and expansion signals to prioritize customer engagement and inform business decisions.

 - Build practical reporting, workflows, and automation that help the team manage a growing customer base. Partner with Finance and Billing Operations to improve the customer experience around credits, commitments, and billing.

 - Bring insights from customers into API planning and take on additional strategic initiatives as business priorities evolve.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years of experience in business operations, strategy and operations, consulting, customer success, account management, or a related role.

 - A track record of taking ambiguous business problems from analysis through implementation, including projects that require coordination across multiple teams.

 - Strong analytical skills: comfortable working with spreadsheets, usage data, and business metrics to identify a problem, test a hypothesis, and recommend an action.

 - Strong relationship skills and a genuine interest in spending a substantial part of your time with customers. You can lead a conversation, understand their priorities, and take responsibility for the follow-up.

 - Curiosity about APIs and AI products, with the ability to learn technical concepts and work effectively with engineering teams.

 - Clear writing, commercial judgment, and the ability to balance ongoing customer relationships with longer-term projects.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Direct customer-facing experience in a B2B technology company, including account management, customer success, partnerships, or solutions work.

 - Experience with API businesses, developer platforms, or consumption-based revenue models.

 - Working knowledge of SQL, CRM systems, or BI tools, and experience automating recurring analysis or workflows.

jobs.title: Global Workplace Business Operations Lead
jobs.description:
OVERVIEW

The Workplace Experience team powers and connects the workday for all Perplexity employees across our global offices.

We are hospitality and experience-driven at the core. We are made up of People people, meaning that we love supporting each other and all of the People in our workplace. We take on the good and the bad with optimism and with a positive, kind approach to solving problems, dealing with the obstacles handed to us, and proactively creating good around us.  We think about each moment through the lens of our colleagues (our customers) so that we can create thoughtful and memorable experiences no matter what task we have at hand.

As our Global Workplace Business Operations Lead, you will manage the business operations and cross-functional program delivery that enable our global Workplace Experience team to scale. In collaboration with the Head of Workplace Experience, you will set the operating framework for your areas, make decisions within agreed priorities and approval limits, and remain hands-on in delivering results. You will own the effectiveness of portfolio operating processes and internal project delivery.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the Workplace operating framework: Lead annual and quarterly planning for your areas, translate team strategy into priorities and resource plans, and establish clear decision rights, delivery commitments and measures of success. Resolve sequencing and capacity trade-offs within agreed parameters and recommend when to add people, vendors or technology.

 - Lead internal capital-project delivery: Take accountability for integrated delivery plans across office openings, refreshes and other capital initiatives. Direct the work of external PMs within agreed scopes, align internal workstreams, resolve delivery issues and hold partners accountable for schedule, cost, quality and operational readiness.

 - Own portfolio controls and insight: Establish dependable lease administration, obligation tracking, space and occupancy information, and portfolio reporting. Set data and control standards, ensure actions have owners, and turn trends and risks into recommendations before deadlines or capacity constraints become problems.

 - Drive financial planning and performance: Own the processes and quality of operating and capital forecasts, commitments, actuals and variance analysis in partnership with Finance. Challenge assumptions, recommend corrective actions and investment trade-offs, and give the Head of Workplace Experience a reliable basis for budget and commitment decisions.

 - Set the systems and reporting roadmap: Own business requirements, governance and improvement priorities for workplace tools such as Envoy. Establish useful performance measures, improve data quality, and automate repeatable work while maintaining appropriate controls and keeping processes practical for the team.

 - Lead EHS program governance: Establish a risk-based plan, clear responsibilities and a review cadence with qualified vendors and internal teams. Drive follow-through on assessed obligations and remediation across offices and remote populations, maintain evidence of completion, and escalate material risks without substituting for specialist advice.

 - Set standards for delivery and handover: Own the development and use of project playbooks, planning processes and operational-readiness criteria. Bring together design standards and occupancy requirements, and ensure completed projects transfer to local operations with the documentation, training, vendor arrangements and issue ownership needed to run well.

 - Serve as a senior operating partner: Lead cross-functional operating and project reviews, surface decisions with clear recommendations, and represent your areas with internal and external partners. Drive resolution within your authority, escalate material changes with options, and build accountability without adding unnecessary layers.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - Senior functional leadership: 8+ years in workplace business operations, corporate real estate, facilities programs or a closely related field, with increasing responsibility for complex, multi-site programs and their outcomes. You have operated with substantial autonomy, not only administered plans set by others.

 - Project and program management expertise: You are a project manager at the core. You are quick and agile, but methodical when it comes to planning for, organizing, tracking, and executing on a project in a way that keeps everything and everyone aligned and on task.

 - Relevant delivery depth: You have a record of delivering office buildouts, relocations or capital improvements as an internal owner, with accountability for scope, financial performance, schedules, change control and external delivery partners.

 - Strong financial and analytical judgment: You have experience driving forecasting and reporting processes, challenging assumptions and translating portfolio data into resource or investment recommendations; strong spreadsheet and analytical skills.

 - Experience building an operating framework: You have established planning, governance, performance measures and systems that helped a growing function deliver more predictably. You know when structure improves execution and when it becomes unnecessary process.

 - Leadership across organizational boundaries: You can secure commitments, challenge constructively and resolve competing priorities across teams and vendors. You communicate risks and recommendations credibly to senior leaders and know which decisions to make independently and which to escalate.

 - Hands-on ownership and sound judgment: You can move between portfolio-level trade-offs and project details, deliver through others without losing accountability, handle sensitive information responsibly, and maintain a kind, service-oriented approach under pressure.

 - Helpful, not required: International portfolio experience, workplace technology ownership, EHS program governance, or a relevant project-management credential.

jobs.title: Billing Operations Lead
jobs.description:
Perplexity is looking for an experienced Billing Operations Manager to join our Finance and Accounting team as we scale our enterprise business. You will own the enterprise billing lifecycle, translating complex commercial agreements into accurate, timely invoices and building the processes and controls that support our growth.

This is a hands-on role working closely with Deal Desk, Enterprise Sales, Legal, and Customer Success. The ideal candidate combines strong billing and systems expertise with sound judgement, a customer-focused approach, and the ability to bring structure to a fast-moving environment.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Enterprise and reseller billing: Own enterprise billing operations from customer and subscription setup through recurring invoicing, renewals, amendments, and cancellations, ensuring accurate and timely billing in accordance with executed agreements.

 - Contract review: Partner with Enterprise Sales and Deal Desk to review nonstandard billing terms before contracts are signed, assess operational feasibility, and route exceptions for approval.

 - Complex billing arrangements: Translate approved pricing and contractual terms into billing configurations and schedules, including seat changes, tiered discounting, prorations, co-terminations, prepaid credits, and usage billed in arrears.

 - Billing inquiries and disputes: Serve as the primary point of contact for enterprise billing questions from customers and internal teams. Investigate discrepancies, coordinate approved credits and rebills, and address underlying causes to prevent recurring issues.

 - Reconciliations and close support: Reconcile contract, subscription, and usage data to billing output and investigate any billing discrepancies. Support month-end close and audits through billing completeness checks, reconciliations, and supporting documentation.

 - Integration management: Identifying and resolving any billing system integration failures.

 - Customer Success and renewal support: Partner with Customer Success, Enterprise Sales, and Deal Desk on renewals, expansions, and changes to customer commitments. Prepare seat, usage, and billing analyses; calculate renewal credits and true-ups; and translate approved agreements into accurate subscription, credit, and invoice updates. Coordinate the resolution of billing issues that could delay renewals or disrupt the customer experience.


REQUIREMENTS

 - Bachelor’s degree or higher in Accounting or Finance.

 - 7+ years of experience in billing operations, order management, order-to-cash, revenue operations, or a related finance function, including hands-on ownership of enterprise SaaS or subscription billing.

 - Billing expertise: Demonstrated ability to interpret complex customer agreements and translate them into accurate billing schedules, invoices, and adjustments, including subscription and usage-based arrangements.

 - Systems proficiency: Hands-on experience with NetSuite, Salesforce, tax engines, and subscription or usage-based billing platforms, with the ability to investigate issues across connected systems.

 - Accounting fundamentals: Working knowledge of accounts receivable, deferred revenue, and revenue-recognition concepts, including ASC 606.

 - Resourcefulness, detail-oriented and a motivation for solving problems and finding solutions.

 - Excellent communication skills, as frequent interaction with both internal and external stakeholders will be required.

 - Ability to multi-task and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment.
